item.apple.name: Apple
item.apple.description: Windfall from under an oak. Still good.

item.axe.name: Axe
item.axe.description: A felling axe from the camp. Heavy at the head.

item.berries.name: Berries
item.berries.description: Picked at the edge of the wood, where the light gets in.

item.coin.name: Old coin
item.coin.description: Worn smooth. Older than the village.

item.firewood.name: Firewood
item.firewood.description: Split and tied at the woodcutters' camp.

item.fish.name: Fish
item.fish.description: Fresh from the shallows. Cold to hold.

item.flower.name: Wildflower
item.flower.description: From the meadow. It will not last.

item.honey.name: Honey
item.honey.description: A jar from the hives in the flower meadow.

item.key.name: Iron key
item.key.description: Arne's father's. It opens the chest in the barn yard.

item.mail.name: Mail shirt
item.mail.description: Rings over a padded shirt. Heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy.

item.ore.name: Iron ore
item.ore.description: A lump from the quarry, red where the iron shows.

item.spear.name: Spear
item.spear.description: Left in the old tower by whoever last kept watch.

item.sword.name: Sword
item.sword.description: Arne's own work. Balanced, and sharp.

item.wheat.name: Wheat
item.wheat.description: A sheaf bound for the mill.

item.wool.name: Wool
item.wool.description: A fleece, shed where the flock grazes.

text: Mind the water, the bank gives way.
Anything you need hammered, I am here till dusk.
Nails, hinges, a blade now and then.
The one by the anvil is spoken for. Lift it if you think you can.
As it happens. The quarry west of the crossroads has iron in it - red in the grey.
Bring me a lump and I will make it worth the walk.
West of the crossroads. Red in the grey. You will not miss it.
Good weight on that. It will do.
Here - the key to the chest in the barn yard.
It was my father's. I never had the stomach for what is in it.
Open it. Whatever is in there has waited long enough.
Locked. Someone went to real trouble over it.
The lock gives with a sound like a cough.
Inside: one coin, and a smell of old cloth.
Open, and empty but for the smell of old cloth.
Four arms, and the paint gone from all of them.
The old tower. Nobody keeps watch in it now.
The mill, over the bridge. Follow the cart ruts.
The quarry. Mind the loose stone.
Mehhh.
It stares at you, chewing, entirely unbothered.
Baaa.
It goes back to the grass.
RIVERSIDE - north to the ford, south to the old wall.
A figure with its arms held out, worn smooth by rain.
Nobody here remembers.
Arne says his father called it the Warden, and left it at that.
Holding something, once.
Whatever it was, the rain took that too.
The bucket is down there somewhere.
Cold air comes up off the water.
The coin turns over twice and is gone.
You do not hear it land.
The water is still.
Your coin is down there somewhere, with the bucket.
